DeletionResponse.description:
The in-app acknowledgement.

route has exactly one outcome: it is authenticated, so there is no
code step. Carrying the two-valued model here would publish a
``requested`` the route can never return.

**No row counts and no ``existed`` flag**, however useful they would
be to a client. The in-app route could afford one -- the caller is
authenticated -- and does not take one anyway: two shapes for one
outcome is how the paths start to drift [BR3.1].

decision so the screen can offer the right action without deciding
what ``declined`` means for itself [TC-9].

What a person may change about themselves.

**Name and address only.** A profile write cannot touch the phone
number, which is the login and changes only through the OTP path,
and it cannot touch a lens: a role is computed per request from
owned batches and enrollments and has no stored field to set
[TC-11, D-2].

fails on its least interesting row.

Read one session's roster, with its version [BR1.5].

**The version is what makes a conflict recoverable.** A write
carries a `base_attendance_version` and a stale one is refused

without the current version it cannot compose the next write.

post.description:
Submit a whole roster in one atomic write [BR3.3-BR3.8].

**The other of the two D4 writes carrying
``client_mutation_id``.** A replay returns the ORIGINAL stored
result with 200 and writes nothing; a stale version is refused
with 409 **after** the lens has been resolved, because the
conflict's details carry the current roster.

:param body: The version, the replay key and every seat's mark
:param session: The request-scoped session
:param lens: The teacher lens
:return: The version now in force

put.description:
Write a session's topic [BR2.1].

**One of exactly two D4 writes carrying ``client_mutation_id``**
and a version, because it is one of the two mid-class paths the
device queue covers [§ B.7, NFR5]. The replay key is FORWARDED, not
merely declared: a body that carries the field while the call drops
it leaves this path with no replay protection, and the schema-level
contract test cannot see the difference. ``test_api.py``'s
``test_both_declared_mutation_id_paths_actually_replay`` is what
asserts the forwarding.

:param session_id: The session, from the route path
:param body: The version, the replay key and the topic
:param session: The request-scoped session
:param lens: The teacher lens
:return: The topic version now in force
